findings.title: Unhealthy flusher processes are never killed before a replacement starts
findings.body:
Processes are created from the 'spawn' context, so they are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. That class subclasses `BaseProcess` directly, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False and `process.kill()` is skipped. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally.

Now, when a process is detected as hung, a new process is spawned for the same shards while the old one keeps running. Both flush the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments to Kafka. Hung processes also accumulate with every restart.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or check `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: join() never terminates flusher processes
findings.body:
The same broken `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check is used here, and it is always False for `SpawnProcess`. As a result, `terminate()` is never called on processes that are still running after the timeout.

In addition, when the deadline is exceeded, the `break` at line 341 exits the loop. Every remaining process is skipped and gets neither a wait nor a terminate.

With N processes, a slow shutdown can leave several orphaned flushers still writing to Kafka and Redis during rebalance or exit.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body:
`spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `shard`. Dashboards or queries that group by one tag name will silently miss the other metric.

Also, `flusher_unhealthy` tags `shard` with an individual int, whereas the other metrics tag it with a comma-joined list. The same tag key therefore carries different value semantics.

findings.title: Dead method _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` is never called anywhere. It duplicates the restart logic and could confuse future maintainers, so it should be removed.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body:
The test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top. That makes the added `time.sleep(0.1)`, meant to give flusher threads time to process, do nothing.

The test only passes because `join()` happens to wait for the threads. The comment is misleading, and the assertion on `messages` is potentially racy.

findings.title: CLI default of 1 contradicts the 'process per shard' default in SpanFlusher
findings.body:
`SpanFlusher` and the factory treat `max_processes=None` as "one process per shard". However, the `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1, so production consumers keep a single flusher process unless the flag is explicitly passed.

The class docstring states "Creates one process per shard", which is inaccurate for the default deployment. Either the default or the documentation should be aligned.
